llc.formation_notes: A Certificate of Name Reservation must be obtained before filing (separate fee, amount not verified on an official page). Foreign LLC registration: $150.

annual_report.name: None with the Secretary of State; the Business Privilege Tax Return (Form PPT) is filed with the Department of Revenue only when the privilege tax exceeds $100
annual_report.due: Form PPT (when required) is due on the due date of the entity's federal income tax return (April 15 for a calendar-year single-member LLC reported on Schedule C; March 15 for a calendar-year partnership LLC or S corp)
annual_report.late_penalty: Failure to timely file: 10% of the tax shown due or $50, whichever is greater

state_tax_on_llc.name: Business Privilege Tax
state_tax_on_llc.applies: Every corporation, LLC (including single-member disregarded LLCs) and S corporation doing business in or registered in Alabama
state_tax_on_llc.notes: Tax on Alabama net worth at $0.25 to $1.75 per $1,000 depending on federal taxable income apportioned to Alabama (<$1: 0.25; $1-$200k: 1.00; $200k-$500k: 1.25; $500k-$2.5M: 1.50; $2.5M+: 1.75 per $1,000). For taxable year 2026, no return is required and nothing is due if the tax calculates to $100 or less (the old $100 minimum is effectively eliminated). Maximum $15,000 for S corps, LLEs and disregarded entities; $500 for electing family LLEs.

sources.title: Alabama Form PPT Instructions 2026
sources.quote: For taxable year 2026, taxpayers who would be subject to the minimum tax of one hundred dollars ($100), do not have a filing requirement.

entity_level_taxes.name: Business Privilege Tax
entity_level_taxes.notes: Same net-worth based privilege tax as LLCs (Form PPT), $0.25-$1.75 per $1,000 of Alabama net worth, nothing due if $100 or less, $15,000 maximum.

pte_elective_tax.rate_note: Electing Pass-Through Entity tax (Form EPT) since tax years beginning 2021: S corps and partnerships multiply Alabama Schedule K lines 1-17 by 5 percent; election made by checking the Electing PTE box on a timely Form 20S/65.

sources.title: Alabama Form PPT Instructions 2026
sources.quote: S-corporations, limited liability entities, and disregarded entities must file Alabama Form PPT.

sources.title: Electing Pass Through Entities - Alabama Department of Revenue
sources.quote: Calculate the total of lines 1 through 17 in the Alabama column on Schedule K from the S-Corporation's Form 20S, then multiply this total by 5 percent.

personal_exemption.notes: Standard deduction phases down with adjusted gross income: single $3,000 at AGI up to $25,999, minus $25 per $500 above, floor $2,500 at $35,500+; MFJ $8,500 minus $175 per $500 above $25,999, floor $5,000 at $35,500+ (2026 withholding booklet formula). Dependent exemption $1,000 / $500 / $300 depending on income. Federal income tax paid is deductible on the Alabama return.

sources.title: Individual Income Tax - Alabama Department of Revenue
sources.quote: 2 percent on first $500 of taxable income ... 5 percent on all over $3,000 ... 2 percent on first $1,000 ... 5 percent on all over $6,000

sources.title: What personal exemptions am I entitled to?
sources.quote: Taxpayers using the Single and Married Filing Separately filing statuses are entitled to a $1,500 personal exemption.

estimated_tax.required_if: You expect to owe at least $500 in Alabama tax for 2026 after withholding and credits
estimated_tax.notes: Form 40ES. An older ALDOR FAQ still shows December 15 for the fourth payment; the 2026 40ES instructions use January 15, 2027.

unemployment_2026.notes: Newly liable employers pay 2.70% on the first $8,000 of wages per employee; later rates by experience rating. The FAQ is not dated for 2026 specifically.

local_taxes.name: Occupational tax (occupational license fee)
local_taxes.applies: Persons engaging in a trade, occupation or profession in the city; withheld by employers from wages. The city lists Occupational Tax among the taxes filed through its online system.

notable: No Secretary of State annual report for LLCs; the only recurring state filing is the Business Privilege Tax return, and none is needed when the tax is $100 or less (https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/26fpptinstr.pdf)
Federal income tax paid is deductible on the Alabama return, and the standard deduction shrinks as income rises (https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/whbooklet_0126.pdf)
Cities and counties levy their own business license taxes on gross receipts; ALDOR does not administer municipal licenses (https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/business-privilege-tax/)
uncertain: Birmingham occupational tax rate: widely reported as 1% of gross receipts/compensation (Birmingham Code § 3A-2-33), but the official code host (Municode) could not be loaded and the city site does not state the rate; whether it reaches self-employed people's net earnings was not verified. Other Alabama cities with occupational taxes (Bessemer, Gadsden, etc.) were not checked.
Name reservation fee: the Secretary of State fee schedule and name reservation pages returned 'Access denied' today.

Standard deduction figures come from the 2026 withholding formula, which uses gross income; the Form 40 chart uses AGI with the same dollar amounts per the statute but the 2026 Form 40 chart was not read.
